correctness.rationale: The definition uses full binary scattered-subsequence universality. Greedy arch factorization counts completed arches. At each two-symbol block zero or one arch closes; the table distinguishes all nine states with boundary prohibition 10 or 11 at paired-height zero. A first ascent to a new paired maximum cannot begin in state O, because entering O from elsewhere requires an earlier downstep 11 from above that maximum. Each first ascent is therefore a distinct bad block and max paired height <= defect. This justifies finite 3(d+1) transfer, all endpoint conditions and G_d=eR(zQR)^df; rationality is formal. Exact symbolic matrix checks recover G0..G3. Separate direct enumeration of 82500 paths to semilength 11 and dynamic tally to 80 reproduce those coefficients. Finite tests supplement, rather than prove, the unbounded theorem.

originality.rationale: Originality resides in the Dyck first-ascent/bad-block structural bound, fixed-deficit rationality and the complete first four strata. Adamson et al. (arXiv:2311.10658v1) count universality for regular accepted languages, and Fleischmann et al. (arXiv:2202.07981) establish general arches and nearly universal words but do not provide this Dyck-specific reduction. OEIS A001793 already gives the defect-two numerical sequence, which is explicitly credited rather than presented as new. Closest checks do not imply the full theorem; an unlocated stronger formulation remains possible.
residual_risks: An unpublished or difficult-to-find lattice-path or automata classification could imply fixed-deficit Dyck rationality.
The OEIS d=2 coefficient formula is prior knowledge; no priority or novelty is asserted for that integer sequence.
Database overlap comparisons are best-knowledge, not an exhaustive uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: A fixed loss of subsequence coverage is a natural constrained-sequence invariant. Unlike unconstrained binary words, balanced words require an unbounded stack, so proving that loss d forces ordinary Dyck height <=2d+1 is a substantial structural reduction. The formula yields exact computation at every d and explicit rational profiles through 3; it also proves exponential rarity against Catalan paths. The value is not dependent on claiming a previously known d=2 coefficient sequence as new.
